claims.text: Conventional processing of high-purity ZrB2 requires sintering above 2300 °C to achieve full densification and desired performance.
Spark plasma sintering can fully densify single-phase ZrB2 at approximately 1700 °C.
Suitable SPS parameters include heating rates of several hundred degrees Celsius per minute, approximately 50 MPa uniaxial pressure, and a 5–10 minute hold.
SPS enhances grain-boundary diffusion in ZrB2.
Rapid SPS densification produces a refined ZrB2 microstructure with minimal porosity and controlled grain growth.
Pulsed direct current during SPS accelerates diffusion kinetics at lower temperatures.
Accelerated diffusion permits full ZrB2 densification without extensive grain growth or microstructural degradation.
SPS processing preserves the strong Zr–B and B–B interactions in ZrB2.
Minimal porosity and controlled microstructure improve the oxidation resistance of ZrB2.
Minimal porosity and controlled microstructure mitigate liquid plating-metal corrosion of ZrB2.
ZrB2 produced by SPS at approximately 1700 °C will have mechanical strength and structural integrity comparable to or better than conventionally sintered ZrB2 produced above 2300 °C.
ZrB2 produced by SPS at approximately 1700 °C will have mechanical strength and structural integrity comparable to or better than previously reported lower-temperature specimens.
SPS-produced ZrB2 will exhibit reduced oxidation rates relative to conventionally sintered and prior lower-temperature ZrB2 specimens.
SPS-produced ZrB2 will exhibit better resistance to liquid plating-metal corrosion than conventionally sintered and prior lower-temperature ZrB2 specimens.
Previously reported lower-temperature ZrB2 specimens are vulnerable to oxidation and liquid plating-metal corrosion.
The expected oxidation-performance boundary extends to approximately 1000 °C in air for several hours.
The expected liquid-metal service boundary includes extended exposure to a plating bath near 700 °C.
The predicted performance depends on achieving full densification, minimal residual porosity, and a uniform microstructure.
